current.text: Ja Morant was traded to Portland. Jerome started both of Memphis's preseason games at point guard.
Experts expect him to be Memphis's starting point guard. Projected starters are Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey, with Scotty Pippen Jr. on the bench.
In preseason he shot 50% on about 32% usage, but in only about 17 minutes a game.

He should play more than last season's 23 minutes. One projection is 27 to 28 minutes a game. Coach Tuomas Iisalo uses short stints, keeps minutes down and runs an 11 or 12 man rotation, and only Boozer and Coward are expected to top 30 minutes.

Last season's per-game line came with about 30 to 33% usage, about 70% true shooting and heavy rest on a team that was not trying to win. Experts expect his usage to drop clearly and his efficiency to fall. His 70% potential assist conversion is also unlikely to last.
He is healthy now. A calf injury cost him about three months last season, and his late-season missed games were tank rest.

Experts disagree on his price. Lloyd calls him one of the best sleepers and the best target on Memphis, is happy to take him in the 70s or 80s, and still sees value at Yahoo rank 88. Others say ESPN's price removes the upside and that a top 13 ESPN ranking is far too high even with 30 minutes.
His value drops sharply if he comes off the bench for about 20 minutes.
At 29 he does not fit Memphis's young core, and the team could move off him. Memphis has three 2027 first-round picks to use in trades.
Memphis has a 4-4-4 schedule in weeks 19 to 21 and only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.
Iisalo plays at a very high pace.

durable.text: He is an efficient scorer with an underrated handle and elite feel for angles, despite below-average athleticism.
He is roughly a 40 to 41% three-point shooter, not a 44% one.
Injuries ruined two of his last three seasons, including about three months lost to a calf injury last season.
He is a better category-league player than points-league player.

note: Both sites value him at 8 USD. Yahoo drafters pay only 1.4 USD at rank 88, while ESPN has him at rank 58. That is mid-round value in our 144-player pool. He has no weak category and projects to help AST, 3PM, STL and FT%, so he fits any build, and Memphis's 4-4-4 playoff schedule is a bonus. Bid up to about his 8 USD value, not ESPN-level hype. Early in the season, check that he holds the starting job, reaches 27 or more minutes under Iisalo's short stints, and keeps his efficiency as his usage falls from last season's 30% or more.
